# Bounded Context Canvas — Billing

<!-- generated by ddd define render from ddd/07-define/define.json on <TS>. Edit define.json and re-render; delete this line to protect hand edits. -->

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context id** | `billing` |
| **Owning team** | Founder (`solo`, stream-aligned) |
| **Deployable** | Meal-kit app (`app`, modular-monolith, data store: own; shared with `subscriptions`) |
| **Subdomains** | `billing` |
| **Implementation pattern** | transaction-script (sourcing: buy, investment: low) |
| **Aggregates (candidates)** | — (not a domain model) |

## Purpose

Billing takes the money for a chosen week: whenever meals are chosen it charges the household's card through Stripe and tells the rest of the system the week is paid. It owns no product rules — a failed charge is reported back to subscriptions, which decides what to do.

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| generic | cost-reducer | commodity |

_Strategize rationale_: Charging a card weekly is a solved problem (Stripe, commodity evolution); it moves no goal on its own, so buy the provider and keep our side a transaction script around the adapter. — _future_: Remains generic; revisit only if we move to invoicing B2B customers

## Domain roles

**execution-context** — Execution context around a bought capability: it reacts to meals-chosen and executes the charge through the Stripe ACL; no model of its own beyond the charge record.

## Inbound communication

| Collaborator | Type | Relationship | Message | Kind | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subscriptions (`subscriptions`) | bounded context | customer-supplier | `meals-chosen` Meals Chosen | event | — | — |

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Box** | … | — |

## Business decisions

1. A week is charged exactly once, on meals-chosen; retries are idempotent on subscriptionId+week
2. A declined card pauses the subscription and releases the week

## Outbound communication

| Message | Kind | Via | Payload | Collaborator | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `week-charged` Week Charged | event | — | — | Fulfilment (`fulfilment`) | bounded context | published-language |

## Assumptions

- [define A1] Fixture: metrics are illustrative targets

## Verification metrics

- Business: failed charges retried and resolved within 24h for >95% of weeks
- Boundary: every Stripe call goes through the PaymentGateway ACL (fitness test)

## Open questions

- _None open._

## Quality attributes

_None yet — not a core context at this depth; see `system-context.md`._

# Bounded Context Canvas — Fulfilment

<!-- generated by ddd define render from ddd/07-define/define.json on <TS>. Edit define.json and re-render; delete this line to protect hand edits. -->

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context id** | `fulfilment` |
| **Owning team** | Founder (`solo`, stream-aligned) |
| **Deployable** | Warehouse service (`warehouse`, service, data store: own) |
| **Subdomains** | `fulfilment` |
| **Implementation pattern** | active-record (sourcing: build, investment: medium) |
| **Aggregates (candidates)** | `box` |

## Purpose

Fulfilment turns a paid week into a physical box: it builds the picking list, packs the box in the warehouse and hands it to the courier with tracking, so the household gets what it chose. It never queries subscriptions; everything it needs arrives on week-charged.

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| supporting | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: Packing and shipping must work but a competitor's box arrives just as well; supporting, active-record CRUD over boxes and picking lists, with a possible move to a WMS product later. — _future_: could move to a WMS

## Domain roles

**execution-context** — Execution context: packers act on it directly and it owns the physical box's lifecycle; it consumes week-charged and never queries subscriptions.

## Inbound communication

| Collaborator | Type | Relationship | Message | Kind | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Billing (`billing`) | bounded context | published-language | `week-charged` Week Charged | event | — | — |

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Box** | … | — |

## Business decisions

1. A box is packed only for a charged week
2. A box is shipped only after it is packed; tracking is recorded on shipment

## Outbound communication

| Message | Kind | Via | Payload | Collaborator | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | | | | _nothing goes out to a known collaborator_ | | |

_Also emits (no consumer known yet)_: `box-packed`, `box-shipped`

## Assumptions

- [define A1] Fixture: metrics are illustrative targets

## Verification metrics

- Business: boxes packed within 12h of week-charged for >99% of weeks; mis-picks <0.5%
- Boundary: fulfilment reads recipe/picking data only from the week-charged payload or its own projection

## Open questions

- _None open._

## Quality attributes

_None yet — not a core context at this depth; see `system-context.md`._

# Bounded Context Canvas — Subscriptions

<!-- generated by ddd define render from ddd/07-define/define.json on <TS>. Edit define.json and re-render; delete this line to protect hand edits. -->

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context id** | `subscriptions` |
| **Owning team** | Founder (`solo`, stream-aligned) |
| **Deployable** | Meal-kit app (`app`, modular-monolith, data store: own; shared with `billing`) |
| **Subdomains** | `subscriptions` |
| **Implementation pattern** | domain-model (sourcing: build, investment: high) |
| **Aggregates (candidates)** | `subscription` |

## Purpose

Subscriptions decides which meals each household receives each week and keeps the standing order alive: it opens, pauses and cancels subscriptions and locks a week's choice before the cutoff, so that households keep choosing (G1). It does not charge the card (billing) or pack the box (fulfilment).

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| core | revenue-generator | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: G1 (grow active subscribers) is won or lost on how easily a household chooses and changes its weekly meals; no off-the-shelf subscription product models cut-offs, swaps and pauses the way we need, so this is the decisive core and gets a rich domain model. — _future_: Stays core for the foreseeable future; menu-choice UX is the differentiator (bet B1)

## Domain roles

**execution-context** — Execution context: it owns the subscription aggregate and takes the household's commands directly; the weekly cutoff is enforced here, not downstream.

## Inbound communication

| Collaborator | Type | Relationship | Message | Kind | Via | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subscriber (`subscriber`) | person | user-interaction | `choose-meals` Choose Meals | command | — | — |

_Read models that inform its commands_: **Weekly menu** (`weekly-menu`, informs `choose-meals`, used by subscriber)

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Box** | … | — |

## Business decisions

1. A week can be chosen once; a second choice for the same week is rejected
2. Choices lock at the weekly cutoff; after it, default meals are assigned

## Outbound communication

| Message | Kind | Via | Payload | Collaborator | Type | Relationship |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `meals-chosen` Meals Chosen | event | — | — | Billing (`billing`) | bounded context | customer-supplier |

_Also emits (no consumer known yet)_: `subscription-started`, `subscription-teleported`

## Assumptions

- [define A1] Fixture: metrics are illustrative targets

## Verification metrics

- Business (G1): active subscriptions grow month on month; weekly choice completed by >90% of active households before cutoff
- Boundary: zero cross-module reads of subscription tables from billing/fulfilment (CI check)

## Open questions

- _None open._

## Quality attributes

| Attribute | Priority | Requirement | Scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| consistency | high | A week is chosen at most once | Double submit |

# System context — Meal-kit subscription

## In plain words

We wrote one page per part: what it is for, what it decides, and how we would know it is healthy.

**Decided:** Three pages. Each names the rules it enforces and the words it owns.

**Assumed:** The cutoff time is a business rule that lives in subscriptions and nowhere else.

**Riskiest:** If the cutoff is really a fulfilment rule (when the warehouse must know), it is written in the wrong place.
